text:
Sam: heads-up — saw a weird handoff hit today where a prefix came back as 'not found' for ~30s after a node rebind. likely ghost-key behavior, opening thread to sync on a recovery pattern
Anika: ack. can you paste the logs?
Sam: pasted minimal trace: `svc-kv: handoff OK -> compact-trigger -> tombstone removed -> later read returns missing despite lease`
Li: that sounds like compaction ran without accounting for in-flight recovery tokens. we cleaned tombstones based on slab-level compaction, right?
Chris: yeah compaction currently only checks epoch <= compact_epoch on slab. it doesn't check pending recovery tokens from other nodes.
Marta: i'd prefer we avoid adding network calls into compaction loop. compaction is latency-sensitive in background. maybe we need a sentinel tombstone type that encodes 'recovering'
Anika: +1 sentinel idea. we talked about soft-tombstones before but never formalized cross-tenant sentinel semantics. how would it behave?
Marta: proposal: when a handoff detects a possible stale residency, it writes a 'RECOVERY_TOMBSTONE' with epoch and lease-token. compactor treats it as opaque and only fully deletes once TTL or explicit clear from owning node
Li: how to guarantee it doesn't become permanent garbage? compactor needs a bound. TTLs are fine but risky if owner crashed permanently. need an admin GC path and an operator-visible metric
Chris: we can use epoched sentinel: {type: RECOVERY, epoch: E, owner: node-id, created_at: T}. compactor can skip deletion until epoch > E + grace_window OR owner confirms transfer. also expose metric `recovery_sentinels_count` and `recovery_sentinel_age_p50/p90`
Sam: sounds plausible. what about cross-tenant slabs that are shared? if owner gone and we let it linger, other tenants may see reduced usable capacity (leaky slabs)
Anika: we should add a fast-path reclaim: if node-id hasn't heartbeated for N epochs, background GC can strip RECOVERY->FORCE_DELETE after escalation. add audit log so support can validate before force purge
Li: question: does RECOVERY tombstone affect prefix lookups? i.e., read path needs to treat RECOVERY as 'in-progress' not missing. clients currently treat missing as cache miss -> backend fetch. that backend write could conflict with recovery owner writing back older state
Marta: read path change: return a special error `KV_RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS` to upstream router which can then 1) retry a few ms later or 2) route to fallback region/model variant. keep default policy to wait short (200ms) then fallback
Chris: we should minimize surface area. returning a special error rather than surfacing internal sentinel keeps API contracts stable. router maps `KV_RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS` -> delay+retry politeness policy
Sam: test plan idea: simulate owner crash during handoff, then run compactor aggressively and ensure read path sees `KV_RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS`, after owner rebind we ensure recovery clears sentinel and normal reads resume. add chaos test for slab sharing with 50 small tenants
Anika: let's add metrics for incidence rate and mean resolution time. also a debug endpoint `/debug/kv/sentinels` that lists sentinels (owner, epoch, age) for operators
Li: can we avoid any schema migration? RECOVERY tombstone can reuse existing tombstone record with an extra flag bit and a small metadata blob (epoch, owner). no large index changes
Marta: sounds low friction. implementation notes: write path sets RECOVERY only when handshake indicates remote handoff pending; recovery writes need linearizability if the slab is multi-leader — ensure we hold slab lease while marking; compactor must check slab-lease ownership before deleting RECOVERY entries
Chris: edge case: two nodes simultaneously think they own — split brain. RECOVERY should be idempotent: if new owner writes a normal tombstone after verifying data, it overwrites RECOVERY. we should add telemetry for conflicting-owner-writes
Sam: UI/ops: add alert when `recovery_sentinels_count` rises > X for > Y minutes. also a support runbook: check `/debug/kv/sentinels`, if owner alive, ask to trigger `recover-checkpoint` on owner; if owner dead escalate GC
Anika: canary plan: implement RECOVERY flag in a feature-flagged build, enable on single small shard pool, 24h watch. run load that triggers handoffs and simulated crashes.
Li: one more: prefix rehydration job might see RECOVERY and stop prefill, causing cold reads. ensure prefill defers on RECOVERY to avoid double writes
Marta: noted. prefill should observe `KV_RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS` and switch to wait-retry policy rather than writing.
ops-bot: background-job: canary-run started on shard-pool-7 with feature RECOVERY-TOMBSTONE (run id: canary-2026-03-22-01)
Sam: thanks. i'll open a short RFC draft with the sentinel schema, canary checklist, and runbook updates. ping me for review. :thumbsup:
Anika: thanks Sam — looking forward to the RFC.
Li: adding test cases to the chaos matrix.
Chris: will sketch compactor changes and add gating in the PR.
Marta: i'll own dashboard/alerts and the `/debug/kv/sentinels` endpoint.
Sam: closing thread for now but will post RFC link when ready.
